exposure: Early oral feeding (within 2 hours post-caesarean surgery)
Delayed oral feeding (after bowel movement establishment post-caesarean surgery)
cohort: 400 women undergoing elective or emergency caesarean delivery under spinal anaesthesia at a hospital in India.
finding: Early oral feeding after caesarean delivery is safe and effectively accelerates gastrointestinal recovery, leading to earlier bowel sound detection, flatus, and stool passage, reduced laxative requirements, and overall better patient outcomes compared to delayed feeding.
mod_finding: Early oral feeding is safe and beneficial for mothers who have undergone caesarean delivery, accelerating their gastrointestinal recovery.
